criteriaFindings.evidence: One thick arched caramel eel fillet, compact ivory rice and one continuous olive nori band sit coherently on a complete shallow ivory plate. The food remains recognizable as eel nigiri across native,66px and40px views. No garnish, extra food, scenery, label or ground shadow appears.

Compared at matching132px/66px widths, the candidate has fuller rice and eel volume, a more deliberate rounded fillet edge and a smoother continuous ceramic rim/front thickness. The plate surface is distinct from the rice, and the rice supports the arch. Eel ends remain complete and thick enough to read.

The warm honey/caramel and ivory midtones and smoother ceramic response visibly improve the source. Enlarged glaze and nori remain more detailed/glossy than the plant reference, but at native/66px/40px the highlights resolve into bounded ordered glaze ribbons and the nori reads as a restrained olive separator rather than competing photographic noise. Warm rim reflection stays inside the object; no external bloom, ground cast shadow or imposed horizontal world light is present.

The lower/front nori is dark but retains olive midtone flecks and a wrapped edge, including at66px. It is not a blank black rectangle. Deep brown fillet undersides and tail seams are narrow, coherent and separate from the nori; they explain thickness without merging into a dead mass. Rounded rice clusters remain visible at66px and suggested at40px, with no need for individual grains at CELL32.

True66px standalone and40px bubble-food views retain caramel top, pale rice, olive central band and full plate. Complete48x80px CELL32 reductions retain the compact caramel/pale/dark-band grouping and plate silhouette at16.5px dish width; matching preference food remains separated within the balloon at10px. Actual serving offsets and original seated-customer occlusion are shown honestly alongside an explicitly labeled inspection-only view.
